summary: Kisin and Zhou prove that for an abelian variety A over a number field and a prime v | p > 2 of good reduction, the ℓ-adic Frobenius conjugacy classes in the Mumford–Tate group G come from a single rational class γ ∈ Conj_G(Q), for all ℓ ≠ p (Theorem 1.1). They do this through integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type for strongly acceptable triples at very special parahoric level. The μ-ordinary locus is open and dense and its points lift to special points (Theorem 1.3), and curves through Kottwitz–Rapoport strata over the same residue field with Chin's companions give ℓ-independence at every mod p point (Theorem 1.2). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and fourteen findings are recorded; the proof gaps E10–E12 and E14 have repairs and the rest are misprints. Not formalised.

items.statement: For a Coxeter system cs on a group W, BruhatLE is the reflexive transitive closure of reflection multiplication steps strictly increasing cs.length. The pin supplies a partial order; the affine group and its comparison to the geometric order remain separate.

items.name: Serre–Tate deformation
items.statement: Deformations of an abelian scheme at a characteristic-p point correspond to deformations of its p-divisible group, with the required polarization and prime-to-p levels.

items.statement: For an abelian variety over F_q, Frobenius has integral characteristic polynomial independent of ell different from p, and eigenvalues of absolute value q^(1/2) in every complex embedding on its Tate realization; invert for the dual/geometric convention.

items.statement: Two semisimple continuous characteristic-zero representations with equal Frobenius characteristic polynomials on a dense set are isomorphic over a common algebraically closed coefficient field. The finite-field curve Chebotarev input is an additional C12 contract.

items.statement: For connected reductive G/F with T the centralizer of a maximal breve-F-split torus, set W=N(breve F)/T_0(O_breve F); its translation subgroup is X_*(T)_I and quotient is the relative Weyl group W_0.

api.statement: For a translation the Newton vector is the average of its Frobenius orbit.

items.name: Sigma-straight element
items.statement: An element w of W is sigma-straight when length(w sigma(w)...sigma^(n-1)(w))=n length(w) for all positive n.
items.note: This is not the condition of having minimal length only once.

api.name: KZ.N08.data
api.statement: Expose the predicate for every positive twisted-power length.

api.name: KZ.N08.transport
api.statement: Sigma-conjugacy transports straight-class data only after the representative theorem; do not assert every representative straight.

api.name: KZ.N08.characterization
api.statement: Straightness is equivalent to equality with the Newton-length bound N09.

items.name: Newton criterion for straightness
items.statement: w is sigma-straight iff length(w)=pair(nu_w_dom,2rho_Sigma).
items.note: Import the exact extended-affine Coxeter result.

items.name: Newton centralizer Levi
items.statement: For v in the apartment rational cocharacter space, form M_v generated by T and root groups with pairing(v,alpha)=0; if varsigma(v)=v it descends to F.
items.note: Centralizer descent uses the linear Frobenius action.

api.name: KZ.N10.data
api.statement: Expose the root subgroups with zero pairing and the torus inclusion.

api.name: KZ.N10.transport
api.statement: Compatible conjugation of v conjugates its centralizer Levi.

api.name: KZ.N10.characterization
api.statement: A root subgroup belongs to M_v exactly when its root pairs to zero with v.

items.name: Straight translation has central Levi cocharacter
items.statement: If t_muprime is sigma-straight, M=M_nu(t_muprime) is defined over F and muprime is central in M.
items.note: Equality in the averaged length bound puts every varsigma iterate in one chamber; zero root pairings force centrality.

items.name: Centrality of an absolute cocharacter lift
items.statement: If muprime=w(mu), with mu the projection of an absolute dominant cocharacter mu-tilde, then lambda-tilde=w(mu-tilde) is central in the Levi of N11.
items.note: Average inertia conjugates of nonnegative root pairings and use their zero sum.

items.name: Mu-admissible set
items.statement: Adm(mu) consists of elements w below t_x(mu) in extended Bruhat order for some x in W_0; Adm_J is its image in W_J backslash W slash W_J.
items.note: Use the geometric conjugacy class and the extended-group components.

api.name: KZ.N13.data
api.statement: Expose membership witnesses w<=t_x(mu) and projection to parahoric double cosets.

api.name: KZ.N13.transport
api.statement: Weyl conjugating the initial cocharacter class leaves Adm unchanged.

api.name: KZ.N13.characterization
api.statement: Membership is a finite disjunction of the specified Bruhat inequalities.

items.name: Sigma-conjugacy classes B(G)
items.statement: B(G) is G(breve F) modulo b to g^-1 b sigma(g), equipped with Newton and Kottwitz invariants.
items.note: Rational sigma-conjugacy is weaker than integral sigma-conjugacy.

api.name: KZ.N14.data
api.statement: Expose class projection and representative changes by g^-1 b sigma(g).

api.name: KZ.N14.transport
api.statement: Group maps induce maps on classes and commute with composition.

api.name: KZ.N14.characterization
api.statement: Equality means existence of a sigma-conjugator in the full local field group.

items.name: Straight Weyl classes classify B(G)
items.statement: The map from sigma-conjugacy classes in W to B(G) is surjective, and its restriction to straight classes is a bijection; Newton and Kottwitz invariants classify B(G).
items.note: Supply the original He classification and its group hypotheses recursively.

items.name: Acceptable Newton set B(G,mu)
items.statement: Set B(G,mu)={b: kappa(b)=mu-natural and nu_b <= mu-diamond}, where mu-diamond is the average under sigma_0 and <= is the nonnegative rational coroot order on dominant points.
items.note: This rational order differs from the integral Schubert order in C02.

api.name: KZ.N16.data
api.statement: Expose kappa equality and the dominant rational coroot inequality separately.

api.name: KZ.N16.transport
api.statement: Compatible derived-isogeny maps preserve the acceptable set with transformed mu.

api.name: KZ.N16.characterization
api.statement: A class belongs iff both defining conditions hold.

items.name: Mu-ordinary class
items.statement: A class in B(G,mu) is mu-ordinary when its Newton point equals mu-diamond; the definition does not assume such a class exists.
items.note: The unique maximal acceptable class need not have this point for a non-quasi-split group.

api.name: KZ.N17.data
api.statement: Expose equality of nu_b with mu-diamond as a predicate on B(G,mu).

api.name: KZ.N17.transport
api.statement: N21 transports membership through the specified derived-isogeny maps.

api.name: KZ.N17.characterization
api.statement: If an ordinary class exists, invariant classification makes it unique.

items.name: Unique maximum versus ordinary existence
items.statement: B(G,mu) has a unique maximal element. For quasi-split G a mu-ordinary class exists; for general G maximality alone does not prove ordinary existence.
items.note: Preserve this distinction in every density statement.

items.name: Straight translation representative of the ordinary class
items.statement: Every mu-ordinary class is represented by a lift of a sigma-straight t_muprime for muprime in W_0(mu).
items.note: Use an admissible straight representative and equality of the Newton-length upper bounds.

items.name: Ordinary existence under a derived isogeny
items.statement: If f:G to Gprime induces an isogeny of derived groups and carries mu to muprime, B(G,mu) has an ordinary class iff B(Gprime,muprime) does.
items.note: Central directions are controlled by Kottwitz invariants.

items.name: Ordinary membership under a derived isogeny
items.statement: Under N20, b in B(G,mu) is ordinary iff f(b) is ordinary.
items.note: A kernel central direction cannot be a nonzero coroot-cone difference.

items.name: Full fixer and connected parahoric
items.statement: For a bounded building subset Xi use the smooth affine full fixer tilde-G_Xi and its connected parahoric G_Xi; integral G_Xi points are fixer points in the kernel of tilde-kappa. For a facet use its associated parahoric.
items.note: The paper's connected-parahoric condition additionally says some full point fixer equals the parahoric.

api.name: KZ.N22.data
api.statement: Expose the full fixer, identity parahoric, integral-point inclusion and reductive special quotient.

api.name: KZ.N22.transport
api.statement: Associated facets and unramified base changes carry the specified models compatibly.

api.name: KZ.N22.characterization
api.statement: Parahoric points are the full fixer intersected with ker tilde-kappa.

items.name: Associated parahorics under adjoint identification
items.statement: If a group map induces an adjoint isomorphism, transfer the relevant building point and define the associated parahorics, independently of the lift in the central apartment.
items.note: This does not by itself prove extension of the group map to integral models.

api.name: KZ.N23.data
api.statement: Expose the transferred building point and its associated parahoric.

api.name: KZ.N23.transport
api.statement: Composition of adjoint identifications composes the associated-parahoric correspondence.

api.name: KZ.N23.characterization
api.statement: Different lifts in the central apartment give the same connected parahoric.

uses.how: State model functoriality with its extra hypotheses.

items.name: Parahoric Iwahori decomposition
items.statement: G(O_breve F) backslash G(breve F) slash G(O_breve F) identifies with W_J backslash W slash W_J; the mu-admissible locus is the union of the indexed double cosets.
items.note: Use connected parahoric integral points consistently.

items.name: Ordinary admissible element lies in a translation cell
items.statement: If b is mu-ordinary and belongs to the union of mu-admissible parahoric double cosets, then b lies in the double coset of a sigma-straight translation t_muprime with muprime in W_0(mu).
items.note: The proof imports the precise He, He–Rapoport and He–Zhou strata statements.

items.name: Integral conjugacy of an ordinary admissible element
items.statement: Under N25, b is sigma-conjugate to the chosen translation lift by an element of G(O_breve F).
items.note: Stronger than the B(G) equality; needed for the actual integral deformation.

items.name: Neron lft model of a torus
items.statement: For a torus over the local field F, use its smooth separated locally finite-type Neron model with the Neron mapping property; distinguish it from its connected and finite-type submodels.
items.note: The abelian-variety Neron roadmap does not state this torus lft contract.

api.name: KZ.R01.data
api.statement: Expose the smooth separated lft model and generic-fiber identification.

api.name: KZ.R01.transport
api.statement: A torus homomorphism extends uniquely through the Neron mapping property.

api.name: KZ.R01.characterization
api.statement: Maps from any smooth O_F scheme are determined by their generic-fiber maps to T.

items.name: Finite-type and identity torus submodels
items.statement: Let T_ft have component group the torsion subgroup of X_*(T)_I, and T_0 have trivial component group; both are open submodels of T_lft.
items.note: Do not identify T_ft and T_0 when inertia coinvariants have torsion.

api.name: KZ.R02.data
api.statement: Expose inclusions T_0 into T_ft into T_lft and the corresponding component subgroups.

api.name: KZ.R02.transport
api.statement: Torus maps preserving the component subgroups induce the stated maps of submodels.

api.name: KZ.R02.characterization
api.statement: A component belongs to T_ft iff its inertia-coinvariant label is torsion; T_0 has label zero.

items.name: Torus closure in a split restriction model
items.statement: Choose a finite splitting extension and close T inside the Weil restriction of the split torus Neron model; denote this locally finite-type closure T_c and prove independence of splitting extension in the source construction.
items.note: The source uses the lft model of the splitting torus; componentwise closure must be specified.

api.name: KZ.R03.data
api.statement: Expose the closure immersion and its generic fiber T.

api.name: KZ.R03.transport
api.statement: Passing to a larger splitting extension induces the source's canonical comparison of closures.

api.name: KZ.R03.characterization
api.statement: The closure is the smallest closed lft subgroup of the chosen restriction model with generic fiber T.

items.name: R-smooth torus
items.statement: T is R-smooth when its closure model T_c is smooth. Then this closure identifies with its Neron lft model; the property is unchanged by passage to the completed maximal unramified extension.
items.note: The closure model is locally finite type. Its finite-type open submodel is separately R02.

api.name: KZ.R04.data
api.statement: Expose the smoothness predicate on T_c.

api.name: KZ.R04.transport
api.statement: It is invariant under completed maximal unramified base change.

api.name: KZ.R04.characterization
api.statement: For an R-smooth torus the closure model satisfies the Neron mapping property and identifies with T_lft.

items.name: Closed immersion of Neron lft models
items.statement: A closed immersion of tori T to Tprime with T R-smooth extends to a closed immersion of their Neron lft models.
items.note: R-smoothness is on the source torus.

items.name: Closed immersion of finite-type torus models
items.statement: Under R05, the induced map T_ft to Tprime_ft is a closed immersion.
items.note: Control the torsion kernel in cocharacter coinvariants.

items.name: Weil restrictions of tame tori are R-smooth
items.statement: A product of Res_(K_i/F) T_i with each T_i a tamely split K_i-torus is R-smooth, without requiring K_i/F itself tame.
items.note: This includes the induced tori used in strong acceptability.

items.name: R-smoothness under torus extensions
items.statement: In an exact sequence of tori with R-smooth kernel and quotient, the middle torus is R-smooth.
items.note: Prove the closure and smooth-quotient statements rather than only generic exactness.

items.name: Closed fixer embedding with equal derived groups
items.statement: A closed G to Gprime inducing an isomorphism on derived groups extends to a closed map of corresponding full fixer models if the centralizer of a maximal breve-F-split torus of G is R-smooth.
items.note: An isogeny of derived groups is weaker than the required isomorphism.

items.name: Fixer embedding after field extension
items.statement: If p>2 and the split-torus centralizer is R-smooth, the natural full fixer map into the restriction of scalars of the corresponding fixer over finite K/F is a closed immersion.
items.note: Reduce to rank-one SL2 and SU3; the odd-prime quadratic extension is tame.

items.name: Primitive root-lattice embedding in rank one
items.statement: For the SL2 root subgroup lattices occurring in 2.4.11, the vector pi_F^n in pi_K^(ne-k) O_K, 0<=k<e, is primitive over O_F; it extends to a basis, giving the closed affine-line embedding.
items.note: This is a proof ingredient of R10; refinement removes the reverse dependency.

items.name: Integral kernel of a central torus quotient
items.statement: For a central extension with R-smooth torus kernel Z, take the schematic closure Ztilde in the source parahoric. Its component group is the kernel of X_*(Z)_I to X_*(T)_I.
items.note: The closure can be disconnected.

api.name: KZ.R12.data
api.statement: Expose the schematic kernel closure and its generic central torus.

api.name: KZ.R12.transport
api.statement: Its component map is induced by X_*(Z)_I to X_*(T)_I.

api.name: KZ.R12.characterization
api.statement: Its component group is the kernel of that lattice map in the source's geometric component identification.

items.name: Smooth fppf exact parahoric quotient
items.statement: Under R12, Ztilde is smooth and 1 to Ztilde to G to Gprime to 1 is fppf exact for the associated parahorics.
items.note: Pointwise exactness over the fraction field does not imply this statement.

items.name: Local model triple
items.statement: A triple consists of a connected reductive G/F, a geometric conjugacy class of minuscule cocharacters and a parahoric model G over O_F. A morphism preserves the cocharacter class and the indicated integral level.
items.note: Morphisms of group data need a proved local-model map.

api.name: KZ.M01.data
api.statement: Expose G, the minuscule conjugacy class, the parahoric and reflex field.

api.name: KZ.M01.transport
api.statement: Morphisms preserve both the cocharacter bound and the indicated integral level.

api.name: KZ.M01.characterization
api.statement: Isomorphisms of triples induce inverse local-model maps after compatible reflex-field base change.

items.name: Acceptable reductive group
items.statement: G is acceptable when G_ad is a product of restrictions Res_(K_i/F) H_i with each H_i tamely split. The fields K_i/F need not be tame.
items.note: Strong acceptability of a Shimura datum later is stricter.

api.name: KZ.M02.data
api.statement: Expose the adjoint product decomposition and tame splitting witnesses.

api.name: KZ.M02.transport
api.statement: Products and the permitted restriction-of-scalars decompositions transport acceptability.

api.name: KZ.M02.characterization
api.statement: Acceptability concerns the adjoint factors and permits wild K_i/F.

uses.how: Apply the good embedding existence theorem.

items.name: Local Hodge embedding
items.statement: A faithful representation G to GL(V) containing scalar homotheties is a local Hodge embedding for mu when its cocharacter acts with the two standard weights of the corresponding Grassmannian; keep the source's mu versus mu inverse convention.
items.note: A faithful representation alone does not have minuscule Hodge weights.

api.name: KZ.M03.data
api.statement: Expose the faithful representation, scalar inclusion and two Hodge weight spaces.

api.name: KZ.M03.transport
api.statement: The associated GL conjugacy class is the specified standard Grassmannian cocharacter.

api.name: KZ.M03.characterization
api.statement: The local Hodge condition includes the weight multiplicities, not just faithfulness.

items.name: Integral local model
items.statement: Construct the proper flat O_E-scheme Mloc for the triple, with generic fiber G/P_mu, reduced special fiber and the specified Scholze–Weinstein v-sheaf. For acceptable Hodge type use the KPZ construction.
items.note: The exact representability theorems and source versions remain to be recursively checked.

api.name: KZ.M04.data
api.statement: Expose the proper flat scheme, its generic flag identification and special-fiber strata.

api.name: KZ.M04.transport
api.statement: Its associated v-sheaf agrees with the stated local-model v-sheaf under base change.

api.name: KZ.M04.characterization
api.statement: The local-model scheme is the specified flat integral extension, not arbitrary generic-fiber data.

uses.how: Identify completed deformation rings and singularities.

items.name: Local-model strata and components
items.statement: The geometric special fiber of Mloc has its mu-admissible Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification; its irreducible components are normal and Cohen–Macaulay in the cited construction's range.
items.note: Normality of components is not normality of an arbitrary reducible whole fiber.

items.name: Good integral Hodge embedding
items.statement: Extend the Hodge representation to a closed immersion of the full fixer into GL(Lambda); call it good when the induced local-model map is a closed immersion into the appropriate Grassmannian.
items.note: The Grassmannian records the weight minus-one subspace for the source's local-model cocharacter.

api.name: KZ.M06.data
api.statement: Expose the full-fixer lattice embedding and the closed Grassmannian model map.

api.name: KZ.M06.transport
api.statement: The generic model map matches the flag map induced by the representation.

api.name: KZ.M06.characterization
api.statement: Goodness is the closed immersion condition in addition to the integral group embedding.

uses.how: Compare tensor deformation and local-model rings.

items.name: Existence of a good integral embedding
items.statement: For p>2, an acceptable Hodge-type local model triple with p not dividing the order of pi_1(G_der) and R-smooth centralizer of a maximal breve-F-split torus admits a good integral Hodge embedding.
items.note: Each of the prime-to-p fundamental-group and R-smooth assumptions is retained.

items.name: Closed local-model map under Weil restriction
items.statement: For the finite field extension and the associated parahoric embedding of §3.1, the natural map of local models into the restriction of scalars of the base-changed model is a closed immersion after the specified reflex-field base change.
items.note: Exact field/flatness hypotheses of FHLR5.27 and AGLR7.21 require reconciliation; no arbitrary map of triples is asserted closed.

items.name: Trace symplectic embedding
items.statement: Given the symplectic representation over K used in §3.1, use the trace to F of the alternating form on the direct sum to realize the restriction-of-scalars embedding, preserving a common scalar similitude multiplier.
items.note: The multiplier condition restricts the group: unrelated multipliers do not preserve a single trace form.

api.name: KZ.M09.data
api.statement: Expose the trace alternating form on the restricted vector space.

api.name: KZ.M09.transport
api.statement: For a common scalar multiplier c, trace(psi(gv,gw))=c trace(psi(v,w)).

api.name: KZ.M09.characterization
api.statement: Nondegeneracy follows from separability and the nondegenerate original form.

items.name: Admissible lattice criterion
items.statement: If the full fixer equals the connected parahoric and the embedding is good, the reduced lattice pi_F g Lambda modulo pi_F lies on Mloc exactly when the parahoric double coset of g is indexed by Adm_J(mu).
items.note: Retain the equality of full fixer and connected parahoric.

items.name: Dieudonne tensors and Hodge lattice
items.statement: Fix a p-divisible G_0/k and Frobenius-invariant tensors s_alpha,0 in D(G_0)^tensor lying in filtration zero. Let D_1 be the inverse image of the Hodge filtration in D(G_0); choose an integral tensor lattice U whose stabilizer is the full fixer.
items.note: This includes the chosen identification U tensor W(k) with D, not just an abstract group label.

api.name: KZ.D01.data
api.statement: Expose D, the preimage Hodge lattice, defining tensors and chosen U-comparison.

api.name: KZ.D01.transport
api.statement: Tensor-preserving changes of U-trivialization conjugate the Frobenius matrix and preserve the filtration type.

api.name: KZ.D01.characterization
api.statement: The full integral stabilizer of the defining family is the selected fixer model.

items.name: Tensor orbit deformation ring
items.statement: Inside the completed GL flag deformation ring A take the flat closure of the G-cocharacter orbit; its completed local ring A_G is the completion of Mloc at the given Hodge point when the embedding is good.
items.note: A_G is an actual quotient complete local ring.

api.name: KZ.D02.data
api.statement: Expose A to A_G and the universal completed Hodge filtration.

api.name: KZ.D02.transport
api.statement: The completed good Grassmannian embedding identifies A_G with the corresponding completed local-model ring.

api.name: KZ.D02.characterization
api.statement: A map from A factors through A_G iff it satisfies that closed formal-subscheme condition.

uses.how: Recognize adapted points of the versal family.

items.name: Zink Witt ring and augmentation ideal
items.statement: For the complete local coefficient rings R in §3.2, define hat-W(R)=W(k) plus Witt vectors in the maximal ideal whose coefficients converge to zero adically; I_R is the kernel of its projection to R.
items.note: Ordinary W(R) is not the same coefficient ring.

api.name: KZ.D03.data
api.statement: Expose the residue-field Witt summand, convergent maximal-ideal summand and augmentation ideal.

api.name: KZ.D03.transport
api.statement: Continuous local maps respecting coefficient choices induce the corresponding hat-W maps.

api.name: KZ.D03.characterization
api.statement: Membership in the maximal-ideal summand requires adic convergence of Witt coordinates to zero.

uses.how: Carry the display and tensor torsors.

items.name: Display of a p-divisible group
items.statement: Over hat-W(R), use the finite free module, Hodge submodule and Frobenius/display maps satisfying the display relations; the Hodge submodule contains I_R M and its quotient is finite projective over R.
items.note: Original display axioms and equivalence must be extracted before closure; this item records their consumer contract.

api.name: KZ.D04.data
api.statement: Expose the module, Hodge submodule and Frobenius display maps.

api.name: KZ.D04.transport
api.statement: Base change respects the display relations and the p-divisible realization.

api.name: KZ.D04.characterization
api.statement: The Frobenius linearization on the prescribed Hodge module recovers the display after its normal decomposition.

items.name: Adapted deformation
items.statement: A lift to O_K is (Gtilde,mu_y)-adapted if the tensors extend integrally and Frobenius-invariantly to its hat-W crystal, there is the specified tensor-preserving trivialization, and its generic Hodge filtration is induced by a G-cocharacter conjugate to mu_y.
items.note: The deformation cocharacter mu_y is inverse to the local-model cocharacter in 3.2.5.

api.name: KZ.D05.data
api.statement: Expose integral tensor extensions, trivialization and the generic cocharacter filtration witness.

api.name: KZ.D05.transport
api.statement: Permitted finite extensions O_K to O_Kprime preserve adaptedness with the transported tensors.

api.name: KZ.D05.characterization
api.statement: Adaptedness requires all three data; rational tensor invariance alone is insufficient.

items.name: Frobenius-image tensor torsor
items.statement: On A_G form the image of the Frobenius pullback of the universal Hodge lattice and the torsor of its tensor-preserving isomorphisms to U tensor hat-W(A_G). Under the source assumptions this is a trivial Gtilde-torsor.
items.note: Anschütz's extension theorem replaces the invalid earlier torsor input.

api.name: KZ.D06.data
api.statement: Expose the Frobenius-image module and its tensor-isomorphism torsor.

api.name: KZ.D06.transport
api.statement: Tensor-preserving base change pulls back the torsor and its sections.

api.name: KZ.D06.characterization
api.statement: Two trivializations differ by the corresponding Gtilde element.

items.name: Very good integral embedding
items.statement: Put a=m_A_G^2+pi_E A_G. The good embedding is very good at y when the canonical comparison between the Frobenius-image lattices over hat-W(A_G/a) preserves defining tensors, equivalently descends to the associated Gtilde-torsors.
items.note: KPZ equation 5.2.2 has base change modulo a on BOTH sides; the displayed KZ formula omits it on the right.

api.name: KZ.D07.data
api.statement: Expose the mod-a comparison and its tensor-preservation equations.

api.name: KZ.D07.transport
api.statement: The equations are independent of a chosen defining tensor family via D08.

api.name: KZ.D07.characterization
api.statement: Very goodness is equivalent to descent of the comparison to Gtilde-torsors over hat-W(A_G/a).

items.name: Independence of defining tensors in very goodness
items.statement: If the comparison in D07 preserves one tensor family cutting out Gtilde, it preserves all invariant tensors and hence any other defining family.
items.note: Descend the comparison to the intrinsic tensor-isomorphism torsor.

items.name: Tensor-preserving display section
items.statement: Under acceptability, a good embedding and very goodness at y, choose a section of D06 that reduces to the constant comparison modulo a, and use it to define the universal display.
items.note: The mod-a constraint is the omitted condition repaired in this version.

api.name: KZ.D09.data
api.statement: Expose a torsor section with its prescribed reduction modulo a and induced display.

api.name: KZ.D09.transport
api.statement: Replacing the section by a congruent tensor-preserving section gives the permitted equivalent deformation comparison.

api.name: KZ.D09.characterization
api.statement: Reduction of the section is the canonical constant comparison, not an arbitrary residue-frame choice.

items.name: Versal adapted deformation criterion
items.statement: Under assumptions A, B and C of 3.2.5, the versal p-divisible deformation over A pulls back along a map A to O_K to an adapted deformation iff that map factors through A_G.
items.note: Do not remove very goodness from this theorem.

items.name: Integral crystalline tensors and trivialization
items.statement: For the p-divisible lift with etale tensors cutting out the stated group in 3.3.1, the crystalline tensors are integral, extend canonically to the hat-W crystal and admit a tensor-preserving comparison with the integral etale lattice.
items.note: The displayed tensor product uses breve-Z_p on a Z_p Tate lattice and the wrong tensor label; reconcile against KP18 with Anschütz substitution.

items.name: Generic filtration comes from a group cocharacter
items.statement: Under D11, the generic Hodge filtration is induced by a G-valued cocharacter conjugate to the specified mu_y.
items.note: The comparison is contravariant and includes the chosen embedding into GL(D).

items.name: Cocharacter filtration lifts the special filtration
items.statement: The cocharacter of D12 can be chosen so that its filtration over W(k) lifts the Hodge filtration of G_0.
items.note: Lifting the special filtration is stronger than matching its generic type.

items.name: Adaptedness recognition from comparison tensors
items.statement: A deformation with the prescribed generic G-cocharacter filtration and etale tensors corresponding to s_alpha,0 under the p-adic comparison is adapted.
items.note: Integrality enters through D11, not merely rational comparison.

items.name: Ordinary Levi has connected fixer
items.statement: For ordinary b normalized by integral sigma-conjugacy to sigma(t_muprime), let M be its Newton Levi. Then its associated full fixer equals its parahoric and M(O)=M(breve Q_p) intersect G(O).
items.note: This is a separate coinvariant torsion argument, not automatic for all Levis.

items.name: Central cocharacter filtration reduces correctly
items.statement: The central absolute cocharacter lambda-tilde of the ordinary Newton Levi induces a filtration whose reduction is the Hodge filtration of G_0.
items.note: Check the inverse cocharacter and the pi times lattice convention via torus specialization.

items.name: Sigma-centralizer and its isogeny action
items.statement: J_b(R) consists of g in G(R tensor breve Q_p) satisfying g b=b sigma(g); it acts on the rational p-divisible realization. For the normalized ordinary point J_b(Q_p) lies in its Newton Levi.
items.note: The induced action is in the isogeny category, not generally by integral automorphisms.

api.name: KZ.D17.data
api.statement: Expose the equation g b=b sigma(g) and action on the rational crystal.

api.name: KZ.D17.transport
api.statement: Changing b by sigma-conjugacy conjugates J_b and its action.

api.name: KZ.D17.characterization
api.statement: J_b is the automorphism group of the corresponding G-isocrystal.

uses.how: Lift the entire action up to isogeny.

items.name: Ordinary central-filtration Breuil–Kisin lift
items.statement: Choose a finite field of definition K for lambda-tilde. Form S=W(k)[[u]], the preimage of the central filtration in its Frobenius pullback, trivialize the M-torsor and define a height-one Frobenius using the Eisenstein factor.
items.note: This direct construction assumes A, B and full-fixer equality, not the separate global very-good hypothesis C.

api.name: KZ.D18.data
api.statement: Expose the S-lattice, preimage filtration and height-one Frobenius.

api.name: KZ.D18.transport
api.statement: Specialization to the Dieudonne realization gives back the original F-crystal with defining tensors.

api.name: KZ.D18.characterization
api.statement: The Frobenius cokernel is killed by E(u) and the induced generic filtration is lambda-tilde.

uses.how: Obtain an adapted ordinary lift through P05.

items.name: Ordinary adapted lift exists
items.statement: Under §3.4's acceptable good-embedding and full-fixer-equality assumptions, a mu-ordinary G_0 has an adapted lift over O_K for finite K/breve Q_p with filtration induced by lambda-tilde.
items.note: The source proves existence; uniqueness is not a theorem extracted here.

items.name: Entire sigma-centralizer action lifts rationally
items.statement: The lift D19 carries the action of J_b(Q_p) extending that on G_0 in the category of p-divisible groups up to isogeny.
items.note: Centrality of lambda makes its filtration invariant; classification transports the rational action.

items.name: Shimura stack at non-neat level
items.statement: For arbitrary compact away-p level, define the canonical stack as the quotient of a sufficiently small-level model by its finite level group, with descent independent of the auxiliary subgroup.
items.note: Non-neat levels are needed to retain the chosen Frobenius in §6.

api.name: KZ.S01.data
api.statement: Expose the finite-level group action, quotient objects and maps from neat covers.

api.name: KZ.S01.transport
api.statement: Changing the chosen normal neat subgroup gives canonically equivalent quotient stacks.

api.name: KZ.S01.characterization
api.statement: An object is a compatible level orbit with its descent data, not a point of a coarse orbit set.

items.name: Normal Hodge integral model
items.statement: Given a good global Hodge embedding and full-fixer equality, normalize the closure of the generic Shimura image in the associated Siegel integral moduli problem over the reflex DVR; descend the stack construction from small levels.
items.note: Reuse the candidate Honda–Tate continuation, distinguishing it from generic V6 and PEL M4.

api.name: KZ.S02.data
api.statement: Expose the generic model map, schematic closure, normalization and universal abelian pullback.

api.name: KZ.S02.transport
api.statement: Permitted changes of Hodge embedding compare the same canonical integral model through the proved functoriality theorem.

api.name: KZ.S02.characterization
api.statement: Its generic fiber is the chosen canonical model and normalization is finite in the source setting.

items.name: Global good Hodge embedding
items.statement: For p>2 and acceptable Hodge-type (G,X) with p not dividing pi_1(G_der) and R-smooth maximal-split-torus centralizer, a Hodge embedding extends to a good integral embedding for the source's associated fixer.
items.note: Global symplectic compatibility is additional to local faithful representability.

items.name: Lift-independent crystalline tensors
items.statement: At a special-fiber point of S02, specialize absolute Hodge tensors from any permitted characteristic-zero lift to obtain integral Frobenius-invariant crystalline tensors independent of that lift.
items.note: Import KMPS's singular-base tensor extension; the previous checkpoint is not a proved supplier.

api.name: KZ.S04.data
api.statement: Expose each integral crystalline tensor at the special point.

api.name: KZ.S04.transport
api.statement: All permitted lifts and comparison maps give the same tensor in the fixed crystal.

api.name: KZ.S04.characterization
api.statement: Frobenius fixes these tensors and their stabilizer gives the specified integral group structure.

uses.how: Distinguish branches and compare product isogeny groups.

items.name: Completed normalization branch and adapted ring
items.statement: At neat level and a point where the embedding is very good, the completed unnormalized Hodge closure is a closed subspace of the Siegel versal deformation space containing the adapted local-model deformation ring; a normalization branch is identified through its lift.
items.note: Preserve the distinction between the closure and its normalization.

items.name: Adapted deformation detects the chosen branch
items.statement: Under S05, a deformation factors through the completed normalization branch selected by the characteristic-zero lift iff its p-divisible deformation is adapted with the branch's tensors.
items.note: This requires the actual tensor data, not just the special abelian variety.

items.name: Tensors distinguish normalization points
items.statement: Under S05, points over the same unnormalized point are equal exactly when their crystalline tensors agree in the specified realization.
items.note: Normalization fibers need not be singleton without this condition.

items.name: Tensor-preserving rational isogeny group
items.statement: I_x is the Q-group of invertible rational endomorphisms of the special abelian variety preserving all the defining tensor realizations; polarization similitude is encoded in the tensor group.
items.note: Its Q-points act as quasi-isogenies, not as all integral automorphisms.

api.name: KZ.S08.data
api.statement: Expose the rational endomorphism algebra, tensor equations and invertible locus.

api.name: KZ.S08.transport
api.statement: Realization maps embed its rational points in the corresponding tensor-preserving realization groups.

api.name: KZ.S08.characterization
api.statement: I_x(Q) is exactly the rational quasi-endomorphisms invertible and preserving the tensor family.

uses.how: Lift the full rational isogeny action.

items.name: Special lift at a very good ordinary point
items.statement: For p>2, good Hodge embedding with full-fixer equality, and ordinary x where it is very good, there is a lift of x over a finite extension that is a special point and carries I_x(Q)'s action up to isogeny.
items.note: Serre–Tate lifts the p-divisible deformation; rank equality forces the generic Mumford–Tate group into a torus.

items.name: Ordinary points are very good
items.statement: Under the setup of 4.1, the embedding is very good at a mu-ordinary point.
items.note: The ordinary KR stratum is smooth; reconcile the source's KPZ locator with the acquired version.

items.name: Integral extension property
items.statement: With assumptions A-prime, B-prime, C-prime of §4.1, the pro-away-p integral model has bijective restriction from mixed-characteristic DVR points to generic-fiber points.
items.note: This is a pro-level statement; do not assert properness at every finite level.

items.name: Hodge local-model diagram
items.statement: Under S11, construct the G-torsor over the integral model and its G-equivariant smooth map of relative dimension dim G to Mloc, with level compatibility and stack descent.
items.note: It identifies local singularities through smooth maps, not a global isomorphism to Mloc.

api.name: KZ.S12.data
api.statement: Expose the G-torsor projection and equivariant smooth map to Mloc.

api.name: KZ.S12.transport
api.statement: Level transition pulls back both maps and their equivariance diagrams.

api.name: KZ.S12.characterization
api.statement: The torsor is locally a product with G and the local-model map has relative dimension dim G.

uses.how: Transport local-model geometry to integral models.

items.name: Compact central torus Zc
items.statement: For Hodge-type G, let Zc_G be generated by the maximal compact subtorus of Z_G over Q and the center of G_der, and then base change to Q_p where required.
items.note: Retain the finite derived-center contribution.

api.name: KZ.S13.data
api.statement: Expose the compact central subtorus and the generated subgroup with Z_(G_der).

api.name: KZ.S13.transport
api.statement: Central datum morphisms induce the compatible maps of these subgroups.

api.name: KZ.S13.characterization
api.statement: Its generic construction includes the finite derived center as well as the compact connected torus.

items.name: Strongly acceptable Shimura triple
items.statement: A Hodge-type datum is strongly acceptable at p when its derived group over Q_p is a product Res_(F_i/Q_p) H_i with each H_i split and Zc is a product of induced tori. A triple further requires a very special parahoric: it stays special over breve Q_p.
items.note: Acceptable, special and very special are different predicates.

api.name: KZ.S14.data
api.statement: Expose the Hodge embedding, split restricted derived factors, induced Zc factors and very-special vertex.

api.name: KZ.S14.transport
api.statement: The auxiliary construction transports the triple to a datum with the stated derived central isogeny.

api.name: KZ.S14.characterization
api.statement: Very special means special after passage to breve Q_p.

uses.how: Pin the exact scope of the geometric results.

items.name: Auxiliary Hodge cover
items.statement: For a strongly acceptable triple construct a Hodge-type datum with central isogeny on derived groups and isomorphic adjoint datum, associated parahoric, prime-to-p fundamental group, globally very good embedding and the stated central torus properties.
items.note: Its separate output properties are S16–S20.

api.name: KZ.S15.data
api.statement: Expose G, X, the derived isogeny, adjoint identification and selected parahoric.

api.name: KZ.S15.transport
api.statement: The construction compares reflex fields and associated parahorics through its stated maps.

api.name: KZ.S15.characterization
api.statement: The auxiliary object satisfies separately S16–S19,S40 and its globally very good embedding.

items.name: Auxiliary derived fundamental group
items.statement: The auxiliary derived fundamental group is a 2-group and is trivial if the adjoint datum has no type D^H factor.
items.note: Separate output of the auxiliary construction.

items.name: Globally very good auxiliary embedding
items.statement: The auxiliary datum has a good integral symplectic Hodge embedding very good at every geometric point of its local model.
items.note: KPZ's construction replaces the earlier version's incomplete deformation input.

items.name: Auxiliary center is R-smooth and quasi-tame
items.statement: The center of the auxiliary G is an R-smooth torus and Zc_G is a product of restrictions of tamely split tori.
items.note: This supplies the integral embedding and quotient arguments.

items.name: Auxiliary abelianized coinvariants are torsion-free
items.statement: For the strongly acceptable case, X_*(G_ab)_I is torsion-free. KZ4.2.3(5) prints torsion; its next lemma and KPZ v1 Proposition 7.2.18 plus p.84 support torsion-free.
items.note: This is an explicit source reconciliation, not an unmarked quotation of the printed statement.

items.name: Very-special fixer is connected
items.statement: If G_der is a product of restrictions of split groups, X_*(G_ab)_I is torsion-free and the parahoric is very special, then its full fixer equals its connected parahoric.
items.note: The statement holds generally with these hypotheses, not only for the auxiliary datum.

items.name: Semidirect quotient star product
items.statement: Let Delta act on H, let Gamma be a Delta-stable subgroup of H, and phi:Gamma to Delta be equivariant for conjugation on Delta, such that phi(gamma) acts on H by conjugation by gamma. Define H star_Gamma Delta=(H semidirect Delta)/{(gamma,phi(gamma)^-1)}; the displayed subgroup is normal.
items.note: The star is this semidirect quotient, not a free amalgamated product. KP18 §4.5.6 was read directly.

api.name: KZ.S21.data
api.statement: Expose the action, equivariant phi, semidirect product and normal quotient map.

api.name: KZ.S21.transport
api.statement: Compatible maps of all three input groups induce a quotient homomorphism commuting with composition.

api.name: KZ.S21.characterization
api.statement: A homomorphism out is a homomorphism from the semidirect product killing every (gamma,phi(gamma)^-1).

items.name: Integral model from neutral components
items.statement: Using the auxiliary connected component, A(G_Zp)-actions and the finite coset set J, form the quotient copies that define the strongly acceptable integral model and descend over the unramified reflex field.
items.note: This construction accounts for all components, not only the identity component.

api.name: KZ.S22.data
api.statement: Expose the finite coset set J, quotient components, level action and reflex descent.

api.name: KZ.S22.transport
api.statement: Refining away-p level commutes with quotient formation and transition maps.

api.name: KZ.S22.characterization
api.statement: The generic fiber identifies with the full canonical Shimura stack, including nonneutral components.

uses.how: Transport canonical lifts to arbitrary components.

items.name: Strongly acceptable local singularity comparison
items.statement: At neat away-p level the integral model of a strongly acceptable triple is etale locally isomorphic to its local model.
items.note: The integral model may be singular.

items.name: Strongly acceptable DVR extension property
items.statement: The pro-away-p integral model for a strongly acceptable triple has the DVR extension property of S11.
items.note: Keep the pro-system and finite-level assertions separate.

items.name: Adjoint local-model diagram
items.statement: Construct over the strongly acceptable model a torsor under the adjoint parahoric with connected special fiber and an equivariant smooth map to Mloc of relative dimension dim G_ad.
items.note: Connectedness is exactly what Lang's theorem uses in the curve argument.

api.name: KZ.S25.data
api.statement: Expose the adjoint-parahoric torsor and smooth equivariant map.

api.name: KZ.S25.transport
api.statement: Base change to the residue field preserves the connected smooth group fiber and the diagram.

api.name: KZ.S25.characterization
api.statement: Rational lifting of a torsor point over F_q follows from Lang for that connected fiber.

uses.how: Lift a marked F_q point to the local-model diagram.

items.name: Extension of maps of Hodge integral models
items.statement: A datum map with compatible associated parahorics and good embeddings as in 4.3 extends to a morphism of integral models.
items.note: Import canonical shtukas and the exact Pappas–Rapoport uniqueness/extension theorem.

items.name: Derived-isomorphic map preserves completions
items.statement: Under S26, if the map induces an isomorphism of derived groups, the induced maps of the neat integral models are isomorphisms on completed local rings.
items.note: Do not weaken isomorphism to central isogeny.

items.name: Neutral-component integral isomorphism
items.statement: The neutral pro-components of the compatible derived-isomorphic Hodge models are isomorphic over the ring of integers of the maximal unramified reflex extension.
items.note: Use finite etale normalization and an etale birational map between normal models.

items.name: Integral Siegel map for an arbitrary Hodge embedding
items.statement: For a strongly acceptable datum and any chosen Hodge embedding, choose the Zarhin self-dual lattice construction and extend the generic map to the appropriate Siegel stack.
items.note: This compares the canonical auxiliary model with the embedding used by the abelian application.

api.name: KZ.S29.data
api.statement: Expose the integral map to the Siegel stack and its universal abelian object.

api.name: KZ.S29.transport
api.statement: On generic fibers it agrees with the map induced by the selected Hodge embedding.

api.name: KZ.S29.characterization
api.statement: Changes introduced by the self-dual lattice construction are tracked by the corresponding isogeny and level maps.

uses.how: Compare canonical models with the abelian representation used in the proof.

items.name: Matched-multiplier fiber product datum
items.statement: Form G_3 as the identity component of G_1 times_(G_ad times G_m) G_2, matching BOTH adjoint images and symplectic multipliers; use V_3=V_1 direct-sum V_2.
items.note: Matching adjoint images alone does not make the direct-sum representation symplectic-similitude.

api.name: KZ.S30.data
api.statement: Expose the two projections, common adjoint map and common multiplier.

api.name: KZ.S30.transport
api.statement: The direct-sum representation carries the common multiplier to that of the sum form.

api.name: KZ.S30.characterization
api.statement: Points are pairs satisfying both equality of adjoint images and equality of multipliers, then restricted to the identity component.

uses.how: Identify A_3 with A_1 times A_2.

items.name: Connected fixer of the fiber product
items.statement: For G_3 of S30 the full fixer equals the parahoric, using the product description of Zc and torsion-free abelianized coinvariants.
items.note: The central subgroup calculation is necessary.

items.name: Good embedding of the fiber product
items.statement: The direct-sum symplectic representation of G_3 extends to a good integral Hodge embedding.
items.note: R-smoothness and the multiplier fiber product enter the closedness argument.

items.name: Ordinary locus of the integral Shimura model
items.statement: Define the locus of points whose associated tensor isocrystal lies in the mu-ordinary class, assuming that class exists; for strongly acceptable triples quasi-splitness ensures existence.
items.note: Use mu inverse when translating from the Hodge cocharacter to B(G,mu).

api.name: KZ.S33.data
api.statement: Expose ordinary membership through the tensor-isocrystal Newton point.

api.name: KZ.S33.transport
api.statement: The definition is independent of a permitted realization trivialization and agrees under N21's maps.

api.name: KZ.S33.characterization
api.statement: The locus consists exactly of points with nu=mu-diamond under the fixed inverse-Hodge convention.

items.name: Ordinary locus is open and dense under normality
items.statement: At neat away-p level, when the special fiber in §4.4 is normal, the mu-ordinary locus is open and dense.
items.note: Ordinary existence and normality remain visible assumptions. (cc-442dc5) Theorem 4.4.4(1) proves the normality of S_K2 from the integrality of the special fibre of the local model.

items.name: Product comparison of universal abelian objects
items.statement: The integral diagram from G_1 left-arrow G_3 right-arrow G_2 maps to the matched-multiplier Siegel diagram, and the pulled-back abelian object A_3 is A_1 times A_2.
items.note: Projector tensors supply the product decomposition.

items.name: Exact isogeny-group sequences for the fiber product
items.statement: At matching points x_i there are exact sequences 1 to C_i to I_x3 to I_xi to 1, with C_i the corresponding central kernel of the datum map.
items.note: Prove surjectivity using tensor projectors and realization centralizers, not arbitrary surjectivity of rational points.

items.name: Ordinary special-point lift for a strongly acceptable triple
items.statement: For p>2, a strongly acceptable triple and a mu-ordinary geometric special point x, there is a finite K/breve Q_p and an integral lift specializing to x whose generic point is special.
items.note: Lift first on the auxiliary neutral component, transport by the completed-local isomorphism and then handle J and Hecke components.

items.name: Rational isogeny action on the ordinary special lift
items.statement: The lift S37 can be chosen so that the action of I_x(Q) on its special abelian variety lifts in the isogeny category.
items.note: No integral automorphism or uniqueness statement is added.

items.name: Ordinary rational Frobenius representative
items.statement: For a mu-ordinary x over F_q in the strongly acceptable setting, there is gamma_0 in G(Q), elliptic over R, conjugate over Q_ell to actual Frobenius for every ell different from p.
items.note: Betti realization of the special lift gives the common representative.

items.name: Auxiliary reflex-field splitting
items.statement: Every place above p of the original reflex field splits in its compositum with the auxiliary reflex field.
items.note: Use the reflex-field condition in the construction of the auxiliary datum.

items.name: Equal-characteristic local-model Schubert realization
items.statement: Identify the special fiber of Mloc with the union of Adm_J(mu) Schubert varieties in the partial affine flag LG/L+G of the equal-characteristic companion reductive group over F_p((t)).
items.note: Keep this scheme realization distinct from the Witt perfection and generic v-sheaf.

api.name: KZ.C01.data
api.statement: Expose the equal-characteristic group, partial flag and Schubert-union isomorphism.

api.name: KZ.C01.transport
api.statement: The stratum labels match Adm_J and Frobenius descent over the chosen finite field.

api.name: KZ.C01.characterization
api.statement: A point lies in a stratum iff its positive-loop orbit has that double-coset label.

items.name: Integral Schubert dominance
items.statement: For dominant inertia-coinvariant cocharacters, lambda <= mu means mu-lambda is a NONNEGATIVE integral combination of positive coroots in Sigma; at a very special parahoric this orders the Schubert strata.
items.note: The generic order is imported from C25. This item is only its Schubert/cocharacter normalization adapter; the root theorem does not depend on local-model geometry.

api.name: KZ.C02.data
api.statement: Expose nonnegative integral coefficients in the coroot difference.

api.name: KZ.C02.transport
api.statement: The integral order implies the rational Newton inequality after tensoring with Q.

api.name: KZ.C02.characterization
api.statement: lambda<=mu iff mu-lambda lies in the monoid generated by the positive coroots.

items.name: Stembridge positive-coroot step
items.statement: If dominant integral lambda<mu in coroot dominance, there is a positive coroot alpha∨ such that lambda+alpha∨ is dominant and <=mu.
items.note: Full Waldspurger proof in Rapoport00 Lemma2.3 reread; its two root-sum/sign leaves are in the pinned Mathlib.

items.name: Frobenius-stable rank-one step
items.statement: For sigma_q-fixed dominant strata lambda<mu in the integral Sigma-coroot order, choose alpha so lambda_prime=lambda+sum_(distinct orbit) sigma_q^i(alpha-coroot) is dominant, strictly higher and <=mu. To identify this combinatorial orbit with the short relative-root rank-one subgroup, retain the Bruhat–Tits valued-root adapter.
items.note: Finite folding proof supplied by C14–C19. Only the local-group normalization/comparison remains gated.

items.name: Split SL2 Schubert curve
items.statement: In the split rank-one factor use x to u_minus(t^-1 x), including x=0, as an affine-line map into the flag; for x nonzero its factorization puts it in the next translation cell.
items.note: Polynomiality is on the loop quotient; the factorization on G_m uses x inverse.

api.name: KZ.C05.data
api.statement: Expose the affine-line map and its value at zero.

api.name: KZ.C05.transport
api.statement: Restricting to G_m gives the stated higher translation cell via the SL_2 factorization.

api.name: KZ.C05.characterization
api.statement: At zero the loop matrix is identity; nonzero parameters land in the next cell.

items.name: Standard SU3 Schubert curve
items.statement: In the unitary rank-one factor with u_minus(c,d) satisfying tau(c)c+d+tau(d)=0, use x to u_minus(0,uprime^-1 x), where tau(uprime)=-uprime, for the standard parahoric case.
items.note: Track the involution and the selected anti-invariant parameter in both ramified and unramified cases.

api.name: KZ.C06.data
api.statement: Expose u_minus(0,uprime^-1 x) and its unitary relation.

api.name: KZ.C06.transport
api.statement: For x in the base field, tau(uprime)=-uprime makes d+tau(d)=0.

api.name: KZ.C06.characterization
api.statement: The determinant is1 and the matrix preserves the specified anti-diagonal Hermitian form.

items.name: Nonstandard ramified SU3 Schubert curve
items.statement: For the nonstandard parahoric SU3(K) intersect s SL3(O_Kprime) s^-1, s=diag(1,1,uprime), use x to u_minus(x,-x^2/2).
items.note: The displayed three-matrix identity certifies the higher-cell factorization; 2 must be invertible.

api.name: KZ.C07.data
api.statement: Expose the polynomial lower-unipotent matrix with c=x,d=-x^2/2.

api.name: KZ.C07.transport
api.statement: Its higher-cell factorization is checked after conjugation by s=diag(1,1,uprime).

api.name: KZ.C07.characterization
api.statement: The relation x^2+d+tau(d)=0 holds for x in the fixed field and odd characteristic.

uses.how: Handle the nonstandard ramified unitary parahoric.

items.name: Rational lift of a positive-loop orbit
items.statement: If a Schubert base point t_lambda is defined over F_q((t)), every F_q point y in its positive-loop orbit is g t_lambda for g in G(F_q[[t]]).
items.note: The printed assumption t_lambda in G(F_q[[t]]) is too narrow for nonzero translations; the proof uses the full loop group. Lang applies to the connected stabilizer intersection model.

items.name: Same-residue-field curve in the local model
items.statement: For a lower-stratum point y over F_q, there exists a smooth geometrically connected curve C/F_q with an F_q-rational point yprime mapping to y and dense open preimage of a strictly higher stratum.
items.note: No extension of the residue field is allowed.

items.name: Rational-point smooth atlas for the relevant stack
items.statement: For the smooth algebraic stack appearing after pulling back the local-model curve and an F_q-rational object, choose a smooth scheme atlas over F_q with an F_q-rational point above that object.
items.note: A smooth atlas without the rational point is insufficient; the exact LMB hypotheses need original-source verification.

items.name: Same-field local curve through a smooth rational point
items.statement: For a scheme smooth over a field k near y in Y(k) and an open U dense on the component of y, there is a smooth geometrically integral k-curve C and c in C(k), with a k-morphism C -> Y sending c to y and with dense inverse image of U. No finite-field extension or projectivity is required.
items.note: Explicit etale-polynomial proof replaces the unresolved use of Poonen3.4 for a nonprojective chart. It only meets one dense open; it makes no multipoint projective Bertini assertion.

items.name: Same-residue-field curve on the Shimura stack
items.statement: For x in a nonmaximal KR stratum over F_q of the strongly acceptable model, there is a smooth geometrically connected C/F_q with xprime in C(F_q) mapping to x and dense open in a strictly higher KR stratum.
items.note: The scheme curve lemma is now proved by etale coordinates. The rational-object stack atlas, Lang/congruence and local-model curve gates remain.

items.name: Group-valued etale local system from the Shimura tower
items.statement: The varying ell-primary level tower gives a G(Q_ell)-torsor local system on the integral Shimura stack away from p; algebraic representations yield lisse coefficient sheaves.
items.note: Carry the actual representation and tensor functor, not just Frobenius polynomials.

api.name: KZ.E01.data
api.statement: Expose the G(Q_ell)-torsor and its tensor functor on algebraic representations.

api.name: KZ.E01.transport
api.statement: Pullbacks along level morphisms and algebraic representation maps commute.

api.name: KZ.E01.characterization
api.statement: Different fiber frames conjugate the G-valued monodromy representation.

items.name: Scheme of semisimple conjugacy classes
items.statement: For connected reductive G in characteristic zero define Conj_G=Spec(O(G)^G); its geometric points correspond to geometric semisimple conjugacy classes and it is canonically identified with T/W after splitting.
items.note: Reuse the candidate ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII; ET.0 supplies rational/stable conjugacy relations and inner twists.

api.name: KZ.E02.data
api.statement: Expose the invariant coordinate algebra, quotient map and geometric T/W comparison.

api.name: KZ.E02.transport
api.statement: Group morphisms induce the compatible maps on invariant quotients where specified.

api.name: KZ.E02.characterization
api.statement: Two geometric semisimple points have the same quotient point iff they are geometrically conjugate.

items.name: Frobenius quotient point
items.statement: For y over F_q and ell different from p, evaluate E01 on geometric Frobenius and project to gamma_y,ell in Conj_G(Q_ell), independent of the fiber trivialization.
items.note: Extending the residue field to F_(q^n) replaces Frobenius by its nth power.

api.name: KZ.E03.data
api.statement: Expose gamma_y,ell and the chosen geometric Frobenius convention.

api.name: KZ.E03.transport
api.statement: Residue extension of degree n induces the nth-power map on the quotient Frobenius class.

api.name: KZ.E03.characterization
api.statement: Changing the geometric-point trivialization conjugates Frobenius and leaves gamma unchanged.

uses.how: Explain why the marked point must keep its residue field.

items.name: Compatible lisse systems on a finite-field scheme
items.statement: An E-compatible system consists of lisse sheaves at finite coefficient places away from p whose det(1-T Frob_x) at every closed point is one polynomial in E[T], under the chosen embeddings.
items.note: Specify geometric Frobenius, finite residue degrees and every coefficient embedding.

api.name: KZ.E04.data
api.statement: Expose the number field E, sheaves at coefficient places and common polynomials at closed points.

api.name: KZ.E04.transport
api.statement: Tensor products, duals and finite coefficient extensions transport the polynomials with the corresponding eigenvalue operations.

api.name: KZ.E04.characterization
api.statement: Compatibility is equality of det(1-T Frob_x) under every specified embedding for every closed x.

uses.how: Construct the companion family used in5.3.5.

items.name: Plain eigenvalues in characteristic p
items.statement: A lisse sheaf is plain of characteristic p when its Frobenius eigenvalues are algebraic and units at every finite place not over p. Plainness is stronger than being a unit only at its own coefficient prime.
items.note: This is the hypothesis that permits Chin's rank-one twisting reduction.

api.name: KZ.E05.data
api.statement: Expose algebraicity and zero valuation at every finite place away from p.

api.name: KZ.E05.transport
api.statement: Products, inverses and algebraic conjugates of plain numbers remain plain.

api.name: KZ.E05.characterization
api.statement: Plainness means the principal divisor is supported only over p.

uses.how: Permit determinant twists without a finite-order assumption on the original sheaf.

items.name: Constant rank-one twist
items.statement: For an ell-adic unit alpha, construct the rank-one sheaf alpha^deg on Spec F_q and its pullback; Frobenius at degree d has eigenvalue alpha^d. If alpha is plain, these form an E-compatible system after adjoining alpha.
items.note: The geometric Frobenius normalization makes alpha=q^-1 the Tate twist.

api.name: KZ.E06.data
api.statement: Expose the rank-one arithmetic monodromy character sending geometric Frobenius to alpha.

api.name: KZ.E06.transport
api.statement: Pullback to F_(q^n) sends Frobenius to alpha^n and products of twists multiply alpha.

api.name: KZ.E06.characterization
api.statement: At a closed point of degree d the polynomial is1-alpha^d T.

items.name: Chin companions for plain sheaves on curves
items.statement: For a smooth curve over F_q and an irreducible or semisimple lisse Qbar_ell sheaf plain of characteristic p, there is a number field E and an absolutely irreducible or semisimple E-compatible system containing it; integer purity is retained if given.
items.note: Reduce determinants to finite order by a plain rank-one twist, apply Lafforgue/Chin4.1, then untwist. No finite-order-determinant assumption is imposed on the original sheaf.

items.name: All algebraic representations have unit Frobenius eigenvalues
items.statement: For the group-valued local system on the Shimura stack, every algebraic representation has ell-adic-unit Frobenius eigenvalues at every closed point, for ell different from p.
items.note: Use tensor constructions and subquotients of a faithful abelian representation; verify all non-p places for E05 rather than only one place.

items.name: Algebraicity of the quotient Frobenius point
items.statement: The faithful Hodge representation induces a finite map Conj_G to Conj_GL(V). Since its image Frobenius point is Q-rational, gamma_y,ell is algebraic over Q, hence belongs to Conj_G(Qbar) under the chosen embedding.
items.note: Finiteness proves algebraicity, not Q-rationality; the bars were checked in the PDF image.

items.name: Curve recognition from an open subset
items.statement: Two semisimple lisse sheaves over a common characteristic-zero coefficient field on a smooth geometrically connected finite-field curve, with matching characteristic polynomials at every closed point of a nonempty open, are isomorphic.
items.note: Prove curve Chebotarev density and semisimple Brauer–Nesbitt. The G_Q-specific finer atlas node does not supply curve density.

items.name: Representation-wise Frobenius independence
items.statement: For y on the strongly acceptable special fiber, any two ell,ellprime different from p and any algebraic representation theta over a common number field of definition have equal characteristic polynomials of theta(gamma_y,ell) and theta(gamma_y,ellprime).
items.note: Induct downward through KR strata: ordinary points give the base; companions compare on the higher-stratum open and curve recognition gives the F_q-rational marked point.

items.name: Algebraic characters separate semisimple classes
items.statement: In a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, two semisimple elements are conjugate if their images have equal characteristic polynomials in every algebraic representation.
items.note: Steinberg's read statement is semisimple-group theory; supply the central-torus/reductive extension explicitly. A single faithful representation is insufficient.

items.name: A proper subgroup misses a conjugacy class
items.statement: If H is a subgroup of a finite group Gamma meeting every conjugacy class, then H=Gamma.
items.note: Let Gamma act on Gamma/H. Every element would fix a coset. Burnside gives average fixed-point count 1; if the index exceeds 1, the identity contributes more than 1, forcing some zero count, a contradiction.

items.name: Rational descent from degree-one primes
items.statement: If a finite number field F/Q has a degree-one prime above every rational prime outside a finite set, then F=Q.
items.note: In a Galois closure every conjugacy class meets Gal(Fprime/F) by Chebotarev, hence that subgroup is the whole Galois group. Do not strengthen degree-one to complete splitting.

items.name: Rational common Frobenius class on a Shimura stack
items.statement: For p>2 and strongly acceptable (G,X,Gpar), every y in its special fiber over F_q has gamma_y in Conj_G(Q) whose image equals gamma_y,ell for every ell different from p.
items.note: First obtain one Qbar class from all representations, then descend its residue field using E14.

items.name: Mumford–Tate group of an abelian variety
items.statement: For A over a number field embedded in C, define MT(A) as the smallest Q-algebraic subgroup of GL(V_B) containing the Hodge cocharacter; equivalently it stabilizes all Hodge tensors of type (0,0).
items.note: Fix homology versus cohomology duality: the source labels H^1 but prints homological Hodge types. Use H^1 and dual Tate with cohomological Hodge types (1,0),(0,1); the printed negative types are recorded in E8. The global Frobenius/multiplier convention still has G-weights.

api.name: KZ.A01.data
api.statement: Expose the smallest rational algebraic group containing mu and the tensor stabilizer description.

api.name: KZ.A01.transport
api.statement: A change of complex embedding transports the group through the inner-twist comparison A03.

api.name: KZ.A01.characterization
api.statement: It is the intersection of rational algebraic subgroups through which the Hodge cocharacter factors.

uses.how: State the group in which Frobenius independence holds.

items.name: Mumford–Tate group is connected reductive
items.statement: The group A01 is connected reductive and supplies a Hodge-type Shimura datum with the chosen polarization.
items.note: This is unconditional and not the Mumford–Tate conjecture.

items.name: Changing complex embedding changes only the inner form
items.statement: Different embeddings of the number field into C give a canonical inner-twist comparison of Mumford–Tate groups via the period-isomorphism torsor, hence canonically identify their conjugacy quotient schemes.
items.note: The group itself need not be canonically identical over Q.

items.name: Common finite field of Galois factorization
items.statement: After a finite extension of the number field, all ell-adic realizations factor through G(Q_ell); factorization for one ell is equivalent to factorization for every ell. Use the minimal such field in the main theorem.
items.note: Deligne's absolute Hodge theorem suffices; equality of algebraic monodromy with G is not assumed.

items.name: Diagonal-multiplier restriction datum
items.statement: For a totally real F/Q, form Hprime=Res_(F/Q) G_F and H=Hprime times_(Res_(F/Q) G_m) G_m using the diagonal multiplier; W=V tensor F carries the trace polarization.
items.note: H is connected and G embeds diagonally in it with the same multiplier.

api.name: KZ.A05.data
api.statement: Expose Hprime, the diagonal-multiplier fiber product H and trace-polarized W.

api.name: KZ.A05.transport
api.statement: The diagonal G map and extension of scalars commute with the symplectic representation.

api.name: KZ.A05.characterization
api.statement: A point of H has the same multiplier in every split restriction factor.

uses.how: Arrange a very special p-level containing Frobenius.

items.name: A compact element becomes hyperspecial-integral
items.statement: For compact g in G(Q_p), after a finite field extension splitting G and the semisimple part's torus, g lies in a hyperspecial subgroup of that extended group.
items.note: Jordan decomposition and dominance in an apartment put the commuting unipotent root coordinates in a hyperspecial fixer.

items.name: Totally real field with the needed local extension
items.statement: Choose a totally real F whose completions at p realize the finite splitting extension used in A06; the resulting diagonal Frobenius lift lies in a very special parahoric of H(Q_p).
items.note: Global approximation/Krasner and the parahoric intersection comparison are separate proof inputs.

items.name: Central-product strongly acceptable enlargement
items.statement: Choose a rational maximal torus T in H with the specified local split-centralizer behavior and containing a suitable Hodge homomorphism; set H_1=H times^(Z_H) T, the quotient by the inverse diagonal center.
items.note: This is a central product, not an undefined fiber product over Z_H.

api.name: KZ.A08.data
api.statement: Expose the quotient of H times T by z to (z,z^-1).

api.name: KZ.A08.transport
api.statement: The inclusions identify their central Z_H actions and induce the datum map.

api.name: KZ.A08.characterization
api.statement: Maps from H and T with agreeing Z_H restrictions descend to the central product.

items.name: The enlargement is strongly acceptable
items.statement: H_1 with its induced Shimura datum and selected very special parahoric is strongly acceptable: its derived factors split after restriction and its Zc is a product of induced tori.
items.note: Verify the compact central torus calculation, not only the derived group.

items.name: Injective Galois-equivariant conjugacy quotient map
items.statement: The maps from G through H to H_1 induce an injection Conj_G(Qbar) to Conj_H1(Qbar), equivariant for Gal(Qbar/Q).
items.note: Diagonal restriction is checked after splitting into factors; then central-product conjugacy adds no identifications on G.

items.name: Frobenius-preserving extension and Shimura realization
items.statement: Choose a p-level open containing the selected lift of geometric Frobenius. Pass to a finite Eprime/E with unchanged residue field at v and Galois image in that level; use the Serre tensor A tensor_Q F up to isogeny and a Galois-stable level orbit to obtain the H_1 Shimura stack point.
items.note: Eprime/E need not be unramified; residue degree one is the necessary condition. Neatness cannot be imposed while retaining the chosen Frobenius automatically.

api.name: KZ.A11.data
api.statement: Expose the extension, selected place, residue-degree-one identification, level and Shimura object.

api.name: KZ.A11.transport
api.statement: The good-reduction Frobenius on the new residue field identifies with the original Frobenius, not a higher power.

api.name: KZ.A11.characterization
api.statement: The chosen Galois subgroup contains the selected Frobenius lift and has image inside the p-level.

uses.how: Descend the common quotient class to the original place.

items.name: Independence of ell for abelian Frobenius classes
items.statement: Let A/E be an abelian variety over a number field embedded in C, with all ell-adic representations factoring through its Mumford–Tate G after the specified finite extension. At any good reduction v of residue characteristic p>2, there exists gamma in Conj_G(Q) agreeing with the geometric Frobenius quotient point for every ell different from p.
items.note: Apply E15 at the H_1 integral reduction; injectivity and Galois equivariance descend the class back to G. No assertion at ell=p or bad reduction is included.

items.name: Real elliptic representative of the common class
items.statement: The common class of A12 lifts to an element of G(R) elliptic modulo the center. Choose a semisimple lift over C, normalize by the central weight scalar, and transfer its compact torus through the appropriate real inner twist.
items.note: Eigenvalues of absolute value one do not put an arbitrary nonsemisimple lift into a compact group.

items.name: Rational representative with one possible exceptional prime
items.statement: Under A12 plus G_der simply connected and G_Qp quasi-split, there exists gamma_0 in G(Q), elliptic over R, conjugate over Q_ell to actual Frobenius for all but at most one prime ell different from p.
items.note: The Kottwitz arithmetic patching input must be proved with these hypotheses; this is stronger than quotient rationality but weaker than conjugacy at every prime.

items.name: Choice of exceptional prime
items.statement: In A14 the possible exceptional prime can be selected from a positive-density set; the rational representative may depend on that choice.
items.note: This flexibility does not produce a single representative working at all primes.

items.name: Adelic level-action group A(G)
items.statement: Define A(G)=(G(A_f)/closure Z(Q)) star_(G(Q)_+/Z(Q)) G_ad(Q)_+, using conjugation and the source topologies.
items.note: Keep topological closures and the plus subgroup from the identity real-adjoint component.

api.statement: Expose the canonical maps from the two star-product factors and the induced level action.

api.name: KZ.S41.transport
api.statement: The inclusions of neutral factors and integral factors induce the named subgroup or comparison maps.

api.name: KZ.S41.characterization
api.statement: Its defining diagonal kernel acts trivially; the action factors through the quotient.

items.statement: Define A(G_Z(p))=(G(A_f^p)/closure Z(Z_(p))) star_(G(Z_(p))_+/Z(Z_(p))) G_ad(Z_(p))_+. Its action extends to the integral model under the source center hypotheses.
items.note: Keep topological closures and the plus subgroup from the identity real-adjoint component.

items.statement: Define A(G)^0 by replacing G(A_f) in S41 by closure G(Q)_+, with the same star-product relation.
items.note: Keep topological closures and the plus subgroup from the identity real-adjoint component.

items.statement: Define A(G_Z(p))^0 by replacing G(A_f^p) in S42 by closure G(Z_(p))_+, with the same star-product relation.
items.note: Keep topological closures and the plus subgroup from the identity real-adjoint component.
