items.name: Closed-point Chebotarev for curves
items.statement: For the finite-field curves and finite etale quotients used here, Frobenius conjugacy classes of closed points satisfy the constant-field degree congruences and are dense in the corresponding arithmetic fundamental-group quotient; export the compact ell-adic density version.
items.note: The exact curve-specific owner is DWP.3, not number-field Chebotarev.

items.name: Closed rank-one flag embedding
items.statement: The map of partial affine flags induced by the simply connected rank-one root subgroup factors through the neutral component of the image group flag and then a proper monomorphism on the component, hence is a closed immersion.
items.note: Keep the neutral-component restriction when passing through the central isogeny.

items.name: Lang surjectivity and rational torsors
items.statement: For a smooth connected algebraic group H over a finite field, the Lang map g to g^-1 Frob(g) is surjective over the algebraic closure; equivalently every H-torsor over that finite field has a rational point.
items.note: Apply first to the finite-type connected stabilizer quotient, with the loop congruence lift checked separately; then to the connected adjoint parahoric special fiber.

items.name: Obtuse roots have a root sum
items.statement: For a finite crystallographic root pairing over a characteristic-zero domain, negative integer pairing and alpha != -beta imply alpha+beta is a root. Apply to the flipped pairing for coroots.

items.name: Distinct simple roots have nonpositive pairing
items.statement: For a finite crystallographic root pairing over a domain, distinct indices in the base support have integer pairing <=0.

items.name: Etale morphisms survive base change
items.statement: Etale is a morphism property stable under arbitrary scheme base change; in the curve square the projection from V times_(A^m) A^1 to A^1 is the base change of V -> A^m.

items.name: Etale means smooth relative dimension zero
items.statement: For a scheme morphism f, Etale f iff SmoothOfRelativeDimension 0 f. This does not supply an etale coordinate chart for an arbitrary smooth scheme.

items.name: Finite Dynkin classification and coordinate models
items.statement: Import the finite reduced crystallographic classification, oriented Cartan matrices and explicit A,B,C,D,E,F,G coordinate models from the upstream root roadmap. Its finite-type classification must not be replanned in this continuation.

items.name: Integral lattice and dominant weight interface
items.statement: Import the integral weight/coweight lattice and dominance interface layered on the upstream root pairing; use the dual pairing when cocharacters are regarded as weights for the coroot system.
items.locator: LieHighestWeight Layers 1–2 and standing integral-weight convention

items.name: Root sums over distinct diagram orbits
items.statement: For a finite based reduced crystallographic root system R and a base-preserving automorphism sigma, let O be an orbit of simple roots and beta_O=sum_(a in O) a. Use each distinct orbit member once. Orbit sums of all roots and their induced coroot functionals define the folded datum after C15–C17; a sigma-average is a different normalization.

api.name: KZ.C14.orbitSum
api.statement: Sum once over the finite orbit, independently of a chosen period of sigma.

api.name: KZ.C14.fixed
api.statement: sigma fixes orbitSum(alpha).

api.name: KZ.C14.positiveCone
api.statement: An invariant nonnegative integral combination of the original simple roots has constant coefficients on each orbit and a unique nonnegative integral expansion in beta_O.

uses.how: Carries the finite orbit or same-field curve construction used below.

items.name: Folding with orthogonal simple-root orbits
items.statement: If R is finite simply laced and every simple-root orbit is orthogonal, the beta_O form a crystallographic root base; every folded root is the sum of one sigma-orbit of roots, and conversely. The folded Weyl group identifies with W^sigma.
items.locator: Stembridge, Folding by Automorphisms (2008), pp1–3, condition(1), Claims1,3,4

items.name: Adjacent folding of even A type
items.statement: For R=A_(2n), n>=1, sigma(e_i-e_j)=e_(2n+2-j)-e_(2n+2-i). Put f_i=e_i-e_(2n+2-i), i<=n. The distinct root-orbit sums are exactly the B_n roots ±f_i and ±f_i±f_j. Their simple roots are f_i-f_(i+1) and f_n. Invariant integral weights have folded simple pairings d_i for i<n and 2d_n at the last node.
items.locator: Derived coordinate calculation for the A_(2n) case excluded by Stembridge condition(1)

items.name: Reduction of general diagram folding to components
items.statement: Decompose R into sigma-orbits of irreducible components. For a component cycle of length c, the return map sigma^c acts on one component and the full fixed subspace is its diagonal transport. The folded root system on the cycle is the corresponding return-map fold, with all squared norms scaled by c. Non-simply-laced irreducible based Cartan diagrams have no nonidentity length-preserving automorphism.

items.name: Invariant integral dominance equals folded dominance
items.statement: Let lambda,mu be sigma-fixed dominant integral weights for R with mu-lambda in the nonnegative integral root cone. They are dominant integral weights for the folded root system of C14–C17, and the same difference is a nonnegative integral combination of its simple roots. The converse holds for such invariant weights.

items.name: Dominant orbit-sum step
items.statement: For a finite based reduced crystallographic root system R, a base-preserving automorphism sigma and distinct sigma-fixed dominant integral weights lambda<mu in integral root dominance, there is a positive root a such that beta=sum_(b in orbit_sigma(a)) b is nonzero, lambda+beta is dominant, and lambda+beta<=mu in integral dominance.

items.name: Polynomial graph avoiding a closed subset
items.statement: For a nonzero h in k[X_0,...,X_(m-1)], m>=1, choose an integer B>=2 strictly greater than every individual exponent in supp(h). Define a:A1_k -> A^m_k by X_i -> T^(B^i). It sends 0 to0, is a closed graph immersion because X_0 maps to T, and h(a(T)) is nonzero.

api.name: KZ.C20.graph
api.statement: Construct the k-morphism with coordinates T^(B^i), for m>=1 and B>=2.

api.name: KZ.C20.markedPoint
api.statement: graph(0)=0 and its first projection is the identity of A1.

api.name: KZ.C20.nonvanishing
api.statement: If each support exponent of h is <B, substitution sends nonzero h to a nonzero polynomial.

uses.how: Carries the finite orbit or same-field curve construction used below.

items.name: Etale coordinates at a rational smooth point
items.statement: If Y is a scheme smooth over a field k near y in Y(k), then some affine neighbourhood V of y admits an etale k-morphism pi:V -> A^m_k. Translating coordinates gives pi(y)=0. If m>=1 choose V integral by restricting to the component through y.
items.locator: Stacks tag054L, statement and full Jacobian proof; regular local component reduction

items.name: Proper boundary has a proper image closure in a coordinate chart
items.statement: For an integral finite-type k-scheme V with etale map pi:V -> A^m and a proper closed subset Z of V, the Zariski closure of pi(Z) has dimension <=m-1. Thus there is a nonzero polynomial h vanishing on pi(Z).
items.locator: Derived finite-type dimension and affine vanishing-ideal adapter

items.name: The component through a smooth rational point is geometrically integral
items.statement: A connected smooth finite-type affine curve over k with a k-rational point is geometrically integral. In a smooth finite-type affine scheme, the unique connected component containing a given rational point is open and closed and retains that rational point.
items.locator: Stacks tag0CDW, statement and proof; smooth connected-component reduction

items.name: Pullback of an avoiding polynomial graph gives the required curve
items.statement: Let V/k be integral smooth affine of dimension m>=1, y in V(k), U a dense open and pi:V -> A^m an etale chart with pi(y)=0. Choose h for Z=V-U by C22 and a by C20. The connected component C through (y,0) of V times_(A^m) A1 is a smooth geometrically integral k-curve, maps to V through y, and meets U in a dense open.

items.name: Integral root-cone dominance
items.statement: For a finite based reduced crystallographic root system R in a real vector space, define lambda <=_R mu when mu-lambda is a nonnegative INTEGER combination of the simple roots of R. Restrict to dominant integral weights only when the theorem needs those additional hypotheses. For cocharacters use the coroot root system.

api.name: KZ.C25.le
api.statement: Construct the relation from nonnegative integer coefficients of mu-lambda in the simple-root basis.

api.name: KZ.C25.iff_coefficients
api.statement: Comparison is equivalent to every difference coefficient being a nonnegative integer.

api.name: KZ.C25.antisymm
api.statement: Opposite comparisons imply equality, by linear independence and nonnegativity.
